items.title: Western Union's Stablecoin Integration
points: Western Union announced plans to offer stablecoin (cryptocurrency pegged to stable assets like the US dollar) transfer services, a major step toward mainstream remittance adoption of crypto.
The move leverages Western Union's existing infrastructure to cut transfer friction and costs.
Stablecoins avoid the price volatility of other cryptocurrencies, a key reason traditional institutions previously avoided crypto adoption.
Positions Western Union to serve an estimated 800+ million unbanked and underbanked people who rely on remittances.

items.title: Market Dynamics and Price Movement
points: Bitcoin and Ethereum volatility reflects competing narratives: institutional adoption momentum versus macro headwinds like inflation and interest rates.
Trading volume patterns show retail and institutional capital flows remain divergent, complicating near-term price forecasts.

items.title: OCC Stablecoin Rule Creates Bank Issuance Pathway
points: Effective January 18, 2026, the OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the US bank regulator) removes the presumption that third-party stablecoin issuer relationships are unlawful.
Direct issuer interest payments remain banned; third-party reward structures will be judged case-by-case.
First regulator to finalize comprehensive GENIUS Act (federal stablecoin law) implementation, setting a template for other agencies, including codified foreign issuer and custody standards.

items.title: Mastercard Adopts x402 Protocol for AI Agent Payments
points: Mastercard AI agents now settle payments on-chain via Coinbase's x402 protocol (a payment standard built into HTTP for automated machine-to-machine transactions).
Marks a major card network's adoption of blockchain-based payment rails.

items.title: Celestia Fibre Upgrade Unlocks 3 Terabytes-Per-Second Throughput
points: Celestia's Fibre mainnet upgrade achieves 3.07 Tb/s data availability (the rate at which transaction data can be made accessible to validators) throughput, the largest upgrade since its 2023 launch.
TIA token gained 59% over four weeks pre-launch, reaching $0.68, as traders anticipated the upgrade.
Extends modular blockchain architecture so rollups and modular chains can validate transactions at scale without storing full history.

items.title: Utah Sues Kalshi Over Prediction-Market Betting
points: Utah sues Kalshi and Susquehanna for $30.6M\u2013$61.2M, alleging illegal gambling fees collected from Utah users through October 19.
First state enforcement action targeting prediction-market market makers rather than just users.
Utah argues rebranding bets as 'event contracts' doesn't change their fundamental nature as gambling; seeks fee refunds, damages, and stricter location verification.

items.title: Morpho Brings Real-World Business Credit On-Chain
points: Morpho Midnight targets the \u20ac4.04 trillion annual global factoring market, letting businesses borrow against accounts receivable with 100% capital utilization.
Uses on-chain proof of receivables, anti-double-financing checks, and compliance access controls to let global capital compete transparently for deal flow.
Broadens DeFi collateral beyond crypto wallet assets to business cash flows, aiming at a $200 trillion on-chain credit market.

sections.title: Morpho Brings Real-World Business Credit On-Chain

sections.title: Utah Attacks Kalshi as Illegal Gambling Despite 'Event Contract' Branding
points: Lawsuit targets Kalshi and Susquehanna entities alleging $30.6M–$61.2M fee collection from Utah users through October 19; demands blocking sports, election, politics, culture, and 'mentions' bets.
First state enforcement against prediction-market market makers: Utah goes beyond users to sue the firms taking opposite side of bets, expanding enforcement scope.
Utah claims rebranding bets as 'event contracts' doesn't change fundamental nature of gambling; seeks return of fees plus damages and tighter location verification.
